nodes.name: WHCD Incident Reconstruction
nodes.description: Persistent discrepancy between official shooting narrative and surveillance footage indicating possible friendly fire by Secret Service at the 2026 White House Correspondents Dinner incident.

nodes.name: Sarah Sidner Original Video Source Verification
nodes.description: Unresolved question of whether Sarah Sidner personally recorded the Erika Kirk "I just want to go home" clip or obtained it from another source.

nodes.name: Erika Kirk Pre-Recorded Statement Authorship and Authenticity
nodes.description: Question of who authored Erika Kirk's pre-recorded 9-minute statement (host suggests Blake Neff), whether it was scripted, and how it was produced.

nodes.name: Trump Truth Social Tweet Authorship/Origin
nodes.description: Question of who authored and pushed send on Trump's April 2026 Truth Social post criticizing Candace Owens (host names Dan Scavino and Natalie Harp as historical senders).

nodes.name: Andrew Kolvet Text Message Full Context Verification
nodes.description: Unresolved question of the complete text message chain shared between Candace and others regarding the December meeting with Erika Kirk; host has publicly authorized release of the full chain.

nodes.name: Erika Kirk Murder Claim Accuracy
nodes.description: Question of whether Candace Owens ever made an explicit on-podcast claim that Erika Kirk murdered Charlie Kirk, and the framing of the December text joke as evidence.

nodes.name: Charlie Kirk
nodes.description: Primary investigative subject of the series; relevant in this episode as the victim whose case is being reopened.

nodes.name: Erika Kirk
nodes.description: Subject of the NYT op-ed (A-2348) and named in the Vance-referenced grief account.

nodes.name: Candace Owens
nodes.description: Victor's stepfather; pled guilty to international drug smuggling conspiracy

nodes.name: Andrew Kolvet
nodes.description: Existing; PR figure under multiple artifact-anchored claims in this episode.

nodes.name: Laura Loomer
nodes.description: Existing; called out Blake Neff via audio artifact (A-2401.1).

nodes.name: Bari Weiss
nodes.description: Publication of Erika Kirk op-ed (A-2348); subject of Charlie Kirk commentary clip (A-2345).

nodes.name: Ben Shapiro
nodes.description: Named by Neff (A-2347) as having reduced involvement with Owens around 2024; subject of op-ed publisher critique (A-2348).

nodes.name: Baron Coleman
nodes.description: Referenced by host as the party who delivered the September 9 Zoom-call conversation to Tulsi Gabbard's office.

nodes.name: Terrell Farnsworth
nodes.description: Referenced as the office to which the Zoom-call conversation was delivered.

nodes.name: Jimmy Kimmel
nodes.description: Family referenced via Usha Vance in Erika op-ed (A-2348).

nodes.name: Susie Wiles
nodes.description: Person Susie Wiles (N-182).

nodes.name: Evan Hill
nodes.description: Washington Post investigative reporter; per the host (28:18), wrote on X that a Secret Service officer fired four times at Cole Allen and that the surveillance footage showed no indication Allen fired his weapon.

nodes.name: Cole Allen
nodes.description: Suspect in the White House Correspondents Dinner incident; per Evan Hill's X post read at 28:18, a Secret Service officer fired four times at him as he charged a security checkpoint.

nodes.name: Sarah Sidner
nodes.description: CNN reporter; per the host (31:35), first shared the clip of Erika Kirk saying "I just want to go home." The host could not confirm she recorded it herself.

nodes.name: David Axelrod
nodes.description: Former top advisor to Barack Obama; named (01:04:56) in Laura Loomer's tweet alleging a secret anti-Trump summit in Rome with Candace Owens, Nick Fuentes and Aubrey Leitch. The host says she did not see him in Rome (01:07:45).

nodes.name: Nick Fuentes
nodes.description: Banned on Instagram/YouTube yet clipped widely; Atlantic also lists him among Elephant Clipping banned subjects.

nodes.name: Aubrey Lech
nodes.description: Former Turning Point USA employee; subject of recorded private investigator visit to her home.

claims.label: Trump publicly criticized Candace Owens calling her "low IQ"
claims.claim: Trump's Truth Social post called Candace Owens "an extremely low IQ individual" and described her attack on the First Lady of France as "despicable."
claims.investigative_direction: Verify the post on Truth Social directly and confirm timestamp; identify authorship via platform logs.

claims.label: Washington Post reported Secret Service officers fired at WHCD suspect
claims.claim: The Washington Post reported surveillance footage shows the moment Secret Service officers fired at the WHCD suspect, Cole Allen.
claims.investigative_direction: Pull the Washington Post article directly; review surveillance footage; verify Secret Service statements.

claims.label: Evan Hill reported no footage of Allen firing weapon
claims.claim: Investigative reporter Evan Hill reported on X that a review of surveillance footage found no indication that Cole Allen fired his weapon at the WHCD incident.
claims.investigative_direction: Pull Evan Hill's X post directly; verify Washington Post's review of footage; cross-reference with official statements.

claims.label: Sarah Sidner first shared clip of Erika Kirk "I just want to go home"
claims.claim: The original public clip of Erika Kirk's "I just want to go home" remark was first shared by CNN's Sarah Sidner.
claims.investigative_direction: Confirm via Sidner's public posts or CNN's records; the host could not confirm Sidner personally recorded the clip.

claims.label: Baron Coleman commented on WHCD media frenzy
claims.claim: Baron Coleman publicly commented on the WHCD media coverage, noting Erika Kirk's emergence as a focal point of the event alongside the ballroom announcement.
claims.investigative_direction: Pull Baron Coleman's clip or post directly for full context.

claims.label: Erika Kirk released a pre-recorded 9-minute video statement
claims.claim: Erika Kirk published a 9-minute pre-recorded video statement, with the remaining portion of her show consisting of Charlie Kirk clips.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify the video directly on Erika Kirk's platforms; review production metadata if available.

claims.label: Erika Kirk claimed she attended WHCD to confront journalists
claims.claim: In her pre-recorded statement, Erika Kirk said she attended the White House Correspondents Dinner specifically to meet journalists who had written about her face-to-face.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify the full statement transcript; identify the Daily Mail journalist mentioned.

claims.label: Erika Kirk claimed Candace Owens accused her of murdering her husband
claims.claim: In her pre-recorded statement, Erika Kirk claimed Candace Owens has publicly accused her of murdering her husband.
claims.investigative_direction: Search Candace Owens' full podcast archive for any explicit accusation of murder; review the December text message chain.

claims.label: Erika Kirk criticized journalists for filming during active shooter
claims.claim: In her pre-recorded statement, Erika Kirk criticized journalists present at the dinner for using their phones to capture video during what she described as an active shooting situation.
claims.investigative_direction: Cross-reference against the Sarah Sidner footage and other journalist videos; verify the timing of any "active shooter" declaration.

claims.label: Erika Kirk criticized Jimmy Kimmel's Melania joke
claims.claim: In her pre-recorded statement, Erika Kirk criticized Jimmy Kimmel's joke about Melania Trump having "the glow of an expected widow."
claims.investigative_direction: Verify Kimmel's original monologue; confirm Erika's quotation is accurate.

claims.label: Taro Farnsworth recorded video at Charlie Kirk shooting scene
claims.claim: Taro Farnsworth recorded himself on video at the Charlie Kirk shooting scene within seconds of the incident, stating "They just shot Charlie."
claims.investigative_direction: Review the Farnsworth video; verify timestamp and original upload context; cross-reference with other scene footage.

claims.label: Andrew Kolvet presented a text message screenshot
claims.claim: Andrew Kolvet publicly presented a screenshot of a text message exchange involving Candace Owens as supporting evidence for Erika Kirk's murder claim.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify the screenshot; obtain the full conversation thread; host has publicly authorized release of the entire chain.

claims.label: Text message contained "why did you murder your husband?" with cry emojis
claims.claim: The text message presented by Andrew Kolvet contained the phrase "why did you murder your husband?" with cry emojis, framed as Candace's planned first question for Erika.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify the exact text against the screenshot; obtain the surrounding messages for context.

claims.label: Candace stated the text was sent in December before meeting Erika
claims.claim: Candace stated the text was sent in December 2025 in response to questions about planned questions for an upcoming meeting with Erika Kirk, framed as a joke referencing the Bari Weiss/Ben Shapiro framing that any question to Erika equaled accusing her of murder.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify the timeline of the meeting and the text; obtain the full chain; verify the Bari Weiss/Ben Shapiro framing.

claims.label: Laura Loomer made a recorded rant containing racial commentary about Candace
claims.claim: Laura Loomer appeared in an audio recording making comments about Candace Owens including racial characterizations and descriptions of personal history.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify the source recording; identify context and any other parties present.

claims.label: Laura Loomer tweeted SPLC paid Candace $500K to communicate David Duke talking points
claims.claim: Laura Loomer tweeted that the Southern Poverty Law Center was paying Candace Owens $500K per year to communicate David Duke talking points.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify the tweet directly; cross-reference SPLC public records; verify any financial relationship.

claims.label: Laura Loomer claimed Candace was at anti-Trump summit in Rome
claims.claim: Laura Loomer tweeted that Candace Owens, Nick Fuentes, and Aubrey Laitsch converged in Rome for a "secret anti-Trump summit," with implied funding from Qatar.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify the tweet; cross-reference against actual attendees in Rome during the relevant dates.

claims.label: Candace traveled to Rome with her family for confirmation
claims.claim: Candace stated she traveled to Rome with her husband and children for her Catholic confirmation by a cardinal in the old Latin rite, and that her priest flew in from London.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify through confirmation records or attendee corroboration; the host referenced her March 2026 announcement.

claims.label: Photo Trump shared was originally posted by Candace in 2019
claims.claim: Candace stated the photo of her that Trump used in his Truth Social post was originally shared by Candace herself on her Twitter account in August 2019.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify the original August 2019 tweet directly on Candace's Twitter/X account.

claims.label: Candace was sick in 2016 from toxic mold exposure in her apartment
claims.claim: Candace stated that in 2016 she became ill with severe symptoms including eczema, hair loss, and cognitive impairment after a toxic mold exposure in her apartment from an HVAC leak.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify via medical records; the underlying photo is the primary artifact anchor.
